title: Phased Onboarding & Capacity KPI Cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical cookbook for running phased customer onboarding (pilot -> private beta -> public beta -> general availability) with a close coupling between capacity planning and the KPIs we use to decide whether to throttle, open, or rollback. Intended audience: product ops, SRE/infra TPMs, solutions eng, and the launch PM.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Map traffic phase -> capacity posture -> 6 leading KPIs -> operational playbook. Keep decisions binary where possible (open/hold/rollback).

Phase definitions:
- Pilot (1–3 customers): manual ramp, dedicated support, high touch. Traffic target 0–1% of expected GA qps; latency SLO relaxed for internal tests.
- Private beta (5–20 customers): feature flags, canary model variants, Dedicated reserved pools optional. Traffic target 1–10% of GA.
- Public beta (open sign-up): autoscale engaged, cost monitors on, billing validations. Traffic target 10–50% of GA.
- GA (full): full routing, observability retention high, SLA comms active.

Core KPIs to track (weekly + real-time where noted):
1) Successful requests per minute (SRPM) — real-time; alert if <95% of expected for 15m after ramp.
2) 95th pct latency (generation) — 95th measured at route/model level; SLO by tier: pilot 1.5s, beta 600ms, GA 350ms.
3) Cost per 10k tokens (USD) — rolling 24h; pre-approve threshold before opening next phase.
4) Model quality regression score (prompt set avg) — daily; regression >3% triggers pause.
5) Error taxonomy ratio (OOMs | timeouts | infra-errors) — alert if infra-errors >1% of requests for 1h.
6) Activation funnel conversion (signup -> key issued -> first 500 requests) — weekly; monitors adoption health.

Capacity mapping table (example rows, keep as CSV lines for quick import):
phase,expected-qps,reserve-gpus,preferred-instance,kv-cache-enabled,batch-window-ms
pilot,5,0.2,GPU-A100-40,yes,20
private_beta,50,1,GPU-A100-80,yes,15
public_beta,400,6,GPU-H100-80,yes,10
ga,1500,24,GPU-H100-173,yes,8

Runbook excerpts (what to do during a suspect degradation):
- Triage owner: on-call infra (SRE) + product ops lead.
- First 3 minutes: check SRPM & 95p latency by model. If latency spike but SRPM steady -> investigate batching/backpressure config.
- 3–10 minutes: verify autoscaler decisions, instance health, and logs for GC/driver restarts.
- 10–30 minutes: if errors persist and cannot be resolved, enact traffic shaping to reserve pool + rollback to previous model variant.
- Communicate: one-sentence status to #launch-ops and post update in JIRA-1234.

Open questions / notes to self:
- How tight should cost-per-10k threshold be for startups vs enterprise customers? (Action: run sims with Redwood Optimize)
- Consider pre-warming KV cache for customers migrating from Dedicated -> Hosted.
- Need a standard CSV import for the capacity table into the Console. (PR: ops-templates#87)

Checklist before opening next phase (must be green):
- [ ] KPIs green for 72h at current traffic level (SRPM, 95p latency, error ratio)
- [ ] Billing tests passed (card auth, invoicing sample)
- [ ] Canary model variant stable for 24h with no >2% quality regression
- [ ] Observability retention set to phase default
- [ ] Runbook assigned and on-call confirmed for next 48h
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (PM, SRE, Solutions Eng, Sales lead)

Owner assignments (examples):
- Product ops lead: Priya Shah (overall decision authority)
- On-call infra: SRE rotation (primary)
- Support escalation: Lena Ortiz
- Billing validation: Marcus Rivera
- Dev tooling import/export: Ethan Brooks

Signals & dashboards to create in Console (names for tickets):
- console/metric/SRPM-by-route (real-time)
- console/metric/95p-latency-by-model (aggregated tags)
- console/metric/cost-per-10k-by-customer-tier
- console/alert/SMOKE-burn-rate (alerts to #launch-ops)

Templates to copy into customer onboarding packet:
- traffic-shape-policy.md (simple JSON toggles for rate-limit thresholds)
- beta-fallback-plan.md (how we rollback model variants gracefully)

Post-mortem anchors (if phase rollback):
- 24–48h immediate blameless post-mortem published to Confluence (link to template above).
- Quantify token-cost delta and re-evaluate recommended model quantization for that customer cohort.

Recent decisions log (short):
- 2026-01-10: Set public beta 95p latency SLO to 600ms after H100 profiling. (PR: perf/521)
- 2026-02-15: Add pre-warm KV cache step to private beta onboarding checklist.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets
- Query SRPM in console: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/metrics/srpm?route=beta
- Force model rollback: rb-tool rollback --route my-route --to-version v1.7.2 --reason "post-beta-quality-regression"

Fragmented ideas (brainstorm):
- Could add a token-bank for free-tier customers to limit sudden token spikes during sign-up days.
- Potential feature flag: dynamic-cost-band that routes to quantized variants when cost-per-10k > threshold.

End of doc.
